newsitem.title: USA: CME feeder cattle end up after setting new highs.
newsitem.headline: CME feeder cattle end up after setting new highs.

text.p: After surging to contract highs which also were nearly two-year highs in all months, CME feeder cattle futures closed higher but off the day's highs.
Live cattle ended mostly higher in generally slow dealings, traders said.

Feeder cattle closed 0.900 to 0.400 cent per lb higher with August up most at 79.500 cents after posting a new contract high of 79.700, the highest level since August 1994. All months set new highs with deferreds trading over 80.000 cents.
Live cattle ended 0.275 higher to 0.100 lower with August up 0.025 at 63.800 cents.

Sliding corn futures provided enough support to boost nearby feeders through early technical resistance and trigger buy stops above 79.000 cents, basis August. Back months had posted new highs earlier when corn values eased, traders said.

"There is a high degree of confidence, not only from the lower corn market today but from the latest six- to 10-day weather forecast showing normal to above normal temperatures to above normal precip through the 4th of July, that the odds are very great that you are going to have a real big corn crop," said Dennis Smith, with LIT division of First Options.

Falling feed costs combined with projections for tightening feeder cattle supplies through the fall ignited demand. Large cow kills last year in turn, reduced feeder cattle supplies and feeder prices subsequently, could rise further, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.19 at $78.34 per cwt, a new high for the move and the highest level since August 18, 1994.
Cargill Investor Services and Term Commodities notably bought late after early demand from E.D.&F. Man. Cargill spread long June live cattle/short January feeders early, . pit sources said.

Carryover technical fund demand and spillover from the rally in feeder cattle kept underpinned cattle futures despite commercial resistance. However, one fund sold August late which pared the gain in that month, traders said.
Expectations by some traders that cash markets will slip through the summer kept a lid on the early fund support. Packers have plenty of fed cattle available, they said.
Rosenthal Collins sold August late while buying October. R.J. O'Brien and E.D.&F. Man bought October with RBH also a seller, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, commission houses bought August 63 puts and 67 calls, pit sources added.
Boneless beef futures found late commercial buying interest but closed at the day's lows. Trimmings also finished lower in the traded months, traders said.
Boneless beef was quoted 0.98 cent per lb lower to 0.50 higher with August off most and distant months bid up. Trimmings ended 0.10 cent lower to 0.20 higher with August off 0.10 at 41.90.
